newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson SA definitive 96 net loss 3.7 billion Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Thomson SA definitive 96 net loss 3.7 billion Ffr.

text.p: French state-owned Thomson SA, the parent company of Thomson Multimedia and holder of the state's stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, said its board adopted definitive 1996 accounts for 1996 and that Thomson SA's net attributable loss was 3.7 billion francs.

The group also said in a statement state representatives had reiterated, "their attachment to continuation and development of Thomson Multimedia" and confirmed talks were continuing with the European Commission to get the go-ahead for a state capital injection.
The statement said Thomson SA would ask for court approval to postpone its annual general meeting until July 31 pending the conclusion of the talks with the Commission in Brussels.
Results for the subsidiary companies have already been released earlier this year and the statement gave no further details on either Thomson Multimedia or Thomson-CSF.
The future of the previous French government's plans to sell the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF is unclear following the return of a left-wing government in a June 1 parliamentary election.

The outgoing government had requested approval from the European Commission -- which vets state subsidies in the European Union -- for a capital injection of more than 10 billion francs for Thomson Multimedia via its parent.
